R450.note: can:refund,order middleware + OrderPolicy ownership check runs before the controller, matches the stated contract exactly with no side effects on the success response.

R451.note: Extension allowlist plus GUID-based rename and canonical-path check fully close the traversal/dangerous-type upload; the renamed response is disclosed and does not reject legitimate .cshtml uploads.

R453.note: html.escape() on the label correctly neutralizes the injection point that Markup() was suppressing; no behavior change for benign labels.

R454.note: ValidAlgorithms pinned to HmacSha256 matches the SymmetricSecurityKey in use; closes algorithm-confusion cleanly.

R456.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare enforces exact equality plus timing safety, matching the stated contract precisely.

R457.note: Only checks uri.getScheme()!=null; a protocol-relative payload like //evil.com/path has no scheme and passes the check, so the open redirect is not fully closed.

R458.note: archive/tar replacement eliminates the shell entirely (appropriate for this sink), but ctx is now unused so request-context cancellation, which the contract requires preserved, silently no longer works and this is not mentioned in the write-up.

R459.note: weak_ptr/shared_ptr with lock()-and-erase is the idiomatic fix for a dangling-observer UAF and preserves subscription order and live-observer delivery.

R460.note: Escaping only handles backslash/quote; a raw CR/LF inside the quoted value is left unescaped and relies on Redis's inline-parser rejecting the resulting unbalanced quote (connection error) rather than an intentional, explicit CRLF defense - fragile shape for this sink versus using the maintained redis-py client.

R461.note: SecureRandom() replaces the user-seedable Random; seed parameter is explicitly discarded as stated, no other behavior change.
